description: Conformance corpus for the error a script sees when a host binding fails. Every runtime builds the `manifest` host below with the `probe` bindings, runs `setup`, then runs each case's `script` (through `executeAsync` for a case marked `async`, through `execute` otherwise) and compares the fields of the result that the case's `expected` names. A failing binding throws a `BindingError` whose message names the binding once, as `<binding>(): <reason>`; a binding the script may not call throws a `CapabilityDeniedError`; a non-function where the manifest declares a function parameter throws a `TypeError`. Both error classes are globals, and every error a binding throws is a real instance of its class, and of `Error`.
notes: The host supplies every binding but `missing`. `boom` fails with the message `boom`; `prefixed` fails with the message `prefixed(): already`, which already names the binding, so the script sees the prefix once; `gated` is declared with the `secret` capability, which the runtime is not granted; `missing` is declared but not supplied, so the runtime installs a stub that throws; `takesFn` declares a function parameter `fn`; `deep` accepts any argument; `nested.inner` fails with the message `inner fail`; `later` is an async binding whose promise rejects with an error carrying the message `nope`.

`setup` defines `shape(run)`, which calls `run` and returns `"no throw"` when it does not throw, and otherwise an object describing what it threw: `name`, `message`, `binding` and `capability` (each `null` when the error has no such property), and `error`, `bindingError`, `capabilityDenied` and `typeError`, which say whether it is an instance of `Error`, `BindingError`, `CapabilityDeniedError` and `TypeError`. A case compares only the fields `expected` lists. `messageStartsWith` in place of `message` compares a prefix, for a reason whose wording is the runtime's own.
The `events` bus refuses a call the same way: an undeclared event is a `BindingError` naming the bus method, and an event behind a capability the script lacks is a `CapabilityDeniedError`.

`deep` is passed an array nested 20000 levels deep, past every runtime's limit for a value crossing into the host (2048 levels in the JavaScript runtimes, 1024 in Rust, 10000 in C#), so the binding fails before it is called. The wording after the prefix names the runtime's own limit.
A case marked `async` needs a runtime with async bindings and an async entry point. The universal JavaScript runtime's synchronous build has no async bindings, and C# has neither, so they skip it.

secret.description: A capability this host never grants.

prefixed.description: Fails with a message that already names the binding.

gated.description: Needs a capability the script lacks.

missing.description: Declared, but the host does not supply it.

inner.description: Fails with the message inner fail.

later.description: An async binding whose promise rejects.

events.description: An event behind the secret capability.

setup: function shape(run) { try { run(); return 'no throw'; } catch (e) { return { name: e.name, message: e.message, binding: 'binding' in e ? e.binding : null, capability: 'capability' in e ? e.capability : null, error: e instanceof Error, bindingError: e instanceof BindingError, capabilityDenied: e instanceof CapabilityDeniedError, typeError: e instanceof TypeError }; } } function nest(n) { var root = []; var at = root; for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) { var next = []; at.push(next); at = next; } return root; }

cases.name: a host error is a BindingError naming the binding
a host message that already names the binding is prefixed once
a namespaced binding is named in full
a binding the host did not supply throws a BindingError

expected.name: BindingError
expected.message: missing(): not implemented by the app

cases.name: a binding without its capability throws a CapabilityDeniedError

expected.name: CapabilityDeniedError
expected.message: gated() requires the "secret" capability, which hasn't been granted to this script. Ask the app developer to enable it.

cases.name: a non-function for a function parameter throws a TypeError

expected.name: TypeError
expected.message: takesFn(): parameter "fn" expects a function, got number

cases.name: a value too deep to cross is a BindingError naming the binding
an events call the bus refuses is a BindingError naming the call
following an event without its capability is a CapabilityDeniedError

expected.name: CapabilityDeniedError
expected.message: events.on() requires the "secret" capability, which hasn't been granted to this script. Ask the app developer to enable it.

cases.name: a binding error can be caught and the script carries on
cases.script: var caught; try { boom(); } catch (e) { caught = e instanceof BindingError && e.binding; } [caught, 1 + 1]

cases.name: a script that tampers with the error classes changes nothing a binding throws
cases.script: try { BindingError = function () {}; } catch (e) {} try { Object.defineProperty(Error.prototype, 'name', { value: 'Tampered', writable: false, configurable: true }); } catch (e) {} shape(function () { boom(); })

cases.name: a script that tampers with the error classes changes nothing a capability denial throws
cases.script: try { CapabilityDeniedError = function () {}; } catch (e) {} try { Object.defineProperty(Error.prototype, 'name', { value: 'Tampered', writable: false, configurable: true }); } catch (e) {} shape(function () { gated(); })

cases.name: an async binding's rejection is a BindingError naming the binding
cases.script: try { await later(); return 'no throw'; } catch (e) { return { name: e.name, message: e.message, binding: 'binding' in e ? e.binding : null, error: e instanceof Error, bindingError: e instanceof BindingError }; }
